topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer opens the session by outlining the lecture objectives and connecting the content to prior practical work on cancer histopathology.

topics.label: Discovery of oncogenes through tumor viruses and transformation assays
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace how the study of transforming retroviruses led to the discovery of cellular proto-oncogenes and established laboratory assays to assess cell transformation.

topics.label: Classification and mechanisms of oncogenes and tumor suppressor genes
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the concepts and molecular mechanisms distinguishing oncogenic activating mutations from tumor-suppressive loss-of-function and dominant-negative mutations.

topics.label: Mechanisms and consequences of genomic instability in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how defects in specific DNA repair pathways, replication machinery, and mitotic chromosome segregation produce sequence and chromosomal instability.

topics.label: Multistep tumor progression and hereditary cancer predisposition
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss how stepwise mutation accumulation drives cancer progression and how inherited germline mutations accelerate this pathway.

topics.label: Lecture wrap-up and reading recommendations
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the session with reading recommendations and an outlook toward the next lecture.
